research_question: In adults (≥18 years) admitted to the intensive care unit — including after cardiac arrest, with acute respiratory failure or ARDS, with septic shock, or receiving mechanical ventilation — does a higher (liberal) fraction of inspired oxygen or arterial oxygenation target, compared with a lower (conservative) target, affect all-cause mortality at the longest follow-up reported?
treatment_label: Higher / liberal oxygen target (e.g. SpO2 >96%, PaO2 >13 kPa, high FiO2, hyperoxia)
control_label: Lower / conservative or low-normal oxygen target
outcome_description: All-cause mortality: number of participants who died from any cause (events) out of the number randomised to each arm (intention-to-treat denominator), taken at the longest follow-up with a death count for all randomised participants (e.g. 180-day, 90-day, hospital discharge; use 28- or 30-day only if nothing later is reported). ICU mortality is used only if no later all-cause death count exists. In factorial trials, all participants assigned a higher oxygen target are compared with all assigned a lower oxygen target, summed across the other randomised factor.
positive_direction: A risk ratio above 1 (positive log RR) means more deaths in the higher/liberal oxygen arm than in the lower/conservative arm — i.e. liberal oxygen is associated with higher all-cause mortality (harm). RR below 1 means fewer deaths with the higher oxygen target.
search_queries: conservative versus liberal oxygen therapy randomised trial critically ill mortality
oxygenation target randomized controlled trial mechanical ventilation ICU mortality
hyperoxia normoxia trial cardiac arrest ARDS septic shock mortality outcome
inclusion_criteria: Randomised controlled trial (including factorial and cluster-randomised designs) comparing a higher/liberal oxygen fraction or arterial oxygenation target with a lower/conservative target

Adult participants (≥18 years, or predominantly adult) who are critically ill or admitted to an ICU, including post-cardiac-arrest, acute respiratory failure/ARDS, sepsis/septic shock, or mechanically ventilated patients
Reports death counts (any cause) per randomised arm, or data from which mortality events and totals can be derived
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic review, meta-analysis, editorial, commentary, opinion, narrative review, protocol without results, or purely theoretical/modelling paper)

No comparison between a higher-oxygen-target condition and a lower-oxygen-target control condition (e.g. single-arm, observational without comparator, or trials of different delivery devices at the same oxygen target)
No quantitative outcome data permitting effect-size calculation (no mortality events and denominators, or no extractable proportions/risk estimates)

Unrelated to the research topic: hyperbaric oxygen therapy, high-flow nasal oxygen versus conventional oxygen as a device comparison, neonatal or paediatric populations, or non-critically-ill/outpatient settings
moderators_to_extract: Patient population (post-cardiac-arrest, ARDS/acute respiratory failure, sepsis/septic shock, mixed ICU, mechanically ventilated)
Oxygenation target definition and separation achieved between arms (SpO2 vs PaO2 vs FiO2; magnitude of difference)
Follow-up timepoint used for mortality (ICU, hospital discharge, 28/30-day, 90-day, 180-day)
Risk of bias / blinding status and single- versus multi-centre design
Publication year and factorial versus simple parallel-group design
effect_size_note: Pool as a risk ratio with a random-effects model (DerSimonian–Laird or REML, with Hartung–Knapp adjustment considered). Events = deaths from any cause at the longest reported follow-up; totals = number randomised to each arm (ITT). Arms assigned by the oxygen target described, not by column position or labelling as 'intervention'. Factorial trials collapsed across the non-oxygen factor. Do not pool serious adverse events, ventilator-free days, organ dysfunction scores, neurological outcome, or length of stay.
